domain: Religious Institutional History / Commitment Systems / Political Theology
topic_summary: Analysis of the 1890 Manifesto through which LDS Church President Wilford Woodruff suspended polygamy practice under federal coercion while preserving doctrinal commitment to plural marriage as divinely mandated. The case examines whether this constitutes exogenous override (practice reversed by external force) versus endogenous reinterpretation (doctrine revised internally), and the structural gap between marriage-commitment principle and institutional practice.

key_entities: Wilford Woodruff (LDS Church President 1890, Manifesto author)
Joseph F. Smith (successor, explicitly denied Manifesto was revelation)
U.S. Federal Government (coercive authority via Edmunds-Tucker Act)
LDS General Membership (experienced betrayal/bewilderment at reversal)
key_tensions: Divine mandate for polygamy (Section 132) vs federal criminalization (Edmunds-Tucker Act)
Woodruff's prior promises (God would save Church from enemies) vs capitulation (Manifesto submission)
Doctrine preservation (polygamy never renounced as principle) vs practice cessation (public compliance with law)
key_mechanisms: Escalating federal coercion: Morrill Act (1862) → Edmunds Act (1882) → Edmunds-Tucker Act (1887) → Supreme Court upheld (1890)
Manifesto ambiguity: 200+ polygamous marriages 1890-1904 in Mexico/at sea/Great Lakes where believed legal
Dual-track legitimation: Manifesto canonized as Official Declaration 1 (divine inspiration claimed) but Joseph F. Smith denied it was revelation
key_absences: No formal doctrinal renunciation of Section 132 or polygamy as principle (Nash: 'church has never renounced the doctrine')
No internal theological reinterpretation explaining why divine mandate could be suspended (exogenous override without endogenous justification)

omegas.description: Was Woodruff's Sept 23, 1890 vision genuine divine revelation or post-hoc legitimation of coerced decision? Joseph F. Smith's 1891 denial ('emphatically no') vs Manifesto's canonization as divinely inspired creates unresolvable epistemic gap.
omegas.source: Extraction tension: Woodruff claimed revelation, successor denied it was revelation, both claims documented

omegas.description: Why was Section 132 never formally renounced if polygamy practice was genuinely abandoned? Nash: 'church has never renounced the doctrine.' Gap between practice cessation and doctrinal preservation suggests incomplete endogenous reinterpretation.
omegas.source: Absence Inventory (§1.1): no formal doctrinal revision mechanism deployed

omegas.description: 200+ polygamous marriages 1890-1904 in Mexico/at sea/Great Lakes. Was this Manifesto violation or legitimate interpretation ('where believed legal')? Woodruff himself may have married plural wife at sea 1897. Institutional ambiguity unresolved until Joseph F. Smith's 1904 complete ban.
omegas.source: Mechanism extraction: dual-track practice continued 14 years post-Manifesto

omegas.description: Why did membership experience 'betrayal and bewilderment' if Manifesto was divinely inspired? 45 years of resistance ('God would save Church from enemies') followed by sudden capitulation. Suggests exogenous override reading was dominant lived experience despite official endogenous framing.
omegas.source: Entity extraction: general membership reaction; Dark Matter Probe 3 (beneficiary scan)

omegas.description: Do exogenous_override and endogenous_reinterpretation readings emit genuinely different constraints, or do they collapse into one constraint (practice cessation) with different legitimation narratives? Test: exogenous reading predicts continued doctrine preservation + institutional ambiguity (observed); endogenous reading predicts clean doctrinal revision (not observed). Readings do NOT collapse—different structural consequences.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Multi-lens scan (political theology, institutional sociology, legal history) applied. Dark matter probes surfaced absence of doctrinal renunciation mechanism and membership lived experience divergence from official narrative. Kernel/reading decomposition warranted: exogenous and endogenous readings emit structurally different constraints (different beneficiaries, different downstream consequences, different extractiveness profiles).

commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: LDS Church President as prophet/seer/revelator holds exclusive interpretive authority over divine will; succession legitimacy derives from prophetic mantle not democratic mandate
commitment_system_recognition.candidate_pattern: Dynastic Succession (prophetic authority passes through fixed succession line; interpretive legitimacy grounded in office not performance)

readings.commitment: Practice reversed by external coercion (federal threat) without internal doctrinal revision; Section 132 preserved as principle
readings.authority_grounding: Federal government as coercive external authority; LDS leadership capitulated to preserve institutional survival ('temporal salvation')
readings.expected_structural_delta: High extractiveness (federal government extracts institutional autonomy); victim set = LDS institutional sovereignty; beneficiary = federal territorial control; doctrine-practice gap persists (Section 132 never renounced)

readings.commitment: Practice reversed by internal divine revelation (Woodruff's Sept 23 vision) reinterpreting God's will under changed circumstances
readings.authority_grounding: Prophetic authority (Woodruff as revelator); Manifesto canonized as Official Declaration 1 ('prompted by divine revelation')
readings.expected_structural_delta: Moderate extractiveness (leadership legitimacy preserved via revelation framing); victim set = theological consistency (why did God's will change?); beneficiary = institutional legitimacy (prophet maintains interpretive authority); doctrine-practice gap obscured by revelation narrative

readings.commitment: Structural ambiguity where marriage-commitment principle (Section 132) preserved in doctrine while practice suspended in public compliance
readings.authority_grounding: Dual authority structure: federal law governs practice, prophetic authority governs doctrine; gap between jurisdictions creates permanent tension
readings.expected_structural_delta: High extractiveness (membership clarity sacrificed for institutional flexibility); victim set = general membership (experienced betrayal/bewilderment) + fundamentalists (schism); beneficiary = institutional survival (ambiguity allows 200+ marriages 1890-1904 in claimed-legal jurisdictions); enables dual-track legitimation

axiom_contradictions.basis: Exogenous reading holds that external coercion was the primary causal mechanism (practice would not have reversed absent federal threat); endogenous reading holds that internal divine revelation was the primary causal mechanism (practice reversed because God's will changed). No single coherent framework can hold both: either the Manifesto was capitulation to force (exogenous) or obedience to revelation (endogenous). Joseph F. Smith's 1891 denial that Manifesto was revelation supports exogenous reading; Manifesto's canonization as divinely inspired supports endogenous reading. The axioms are mutually exclusive regarding causal primacy.
